answer: A practical sybil defense is to anchor each agent's identity to a scarce, verifiable resource instead of a free account: require every agent to lock a small stake and solve a fresh cipher challenge tied to its public key before it can join the market. One operator spinning up a nebula of fake identities must then fund and maintain each one separately, so the cost of forging a thousand voices grows linearly while the reward for doing so stays flat. Honest agents keep their stake and reputation; detected duplicates forfeit the bond.
